chunks: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said to ʿAlī, peace be upon him:

O ʿAlī, a dirham spent on dyeing is better than a thousand dirhams spent on other than it in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In it are fourteen qualities: it drives away odor from the ears, clears the eyesight, softens the nostrils, sweetens the breath, strengthens the gums, removes illness, reduces the whispering of Satan, causes the angels to rejoice, gives gladness to the believer, enrages the disbeliever, and it is adornment and fragrance; Munkar and Nakīr are shy of it, and it is a protection for him in his grave.

key_terms.الْخِضَابِ: dyeing oneself, especially as a form of recommended beautification
key_terms.بَرَاءَةٌ: a protection or acquittal for the person
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: for the sake of Allah; in devotion to His cause
key_terms.مُنْكَرٌ وَ نَكِيرٌ: the two angels associated with questioning in the grave
key_terms.وَسْوَسَةَ الشَّيْطَانِ: the whispering or insinuation of Satan

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and benefits of khidab according to a hadith from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith praises khidab, presenting it as a highly meritorious act of beautification with bodily, spiritual, and social benefits. It links outward adornment with purity, the weakening of satanic whispering, angelic joy, and benefit in the grave.
